caveats: Authority and program overlap are confirmed; SmartStart causation and transactions are not.

conclusions: A source-backed state-to-local implementation architecture overlaps the public SmartStart contributor network.
The overlap establishes access and institutional capacity, not proof that WEF directed a local government, selected a school, or caused a grant or project.

The highest-value next evidence is transactional:applications, award lists, agreements, agendas, contracts, board minutes and implementation documents containing SmartStart, WEF, or identifiable SmartStart program language.
counterarguments: Senior officials often participate in broad workforce initiatives without integrating them into their agencies.
Skills in Sync, Future48 and Kentucky manufacturing projects can arise independently from state economic-development policy.
A name appearing in a public contributor roster does not disclose the person's actual contribution, vote, funding authority or continuing participation.
findings: Susan Corbin is publicly named in the SmartStart contributor roster and directs Michigan LEO, which administers grants and statewide systems connecting school districts, manufacturers, postsecondary providers and local workforce organizations.
Michigan's Skills in Sync pilot begins in August 2026 and funds regional K-12-manufacturing partnership networks; no source reviewed calls it a SmartStart pilot.
Sandra Watson is publicly named in the SmartStart contributor roster and leads the Arizona Commerce Authority while advising the governor on economic policy.

ACA's Future48 network uses multi-million-dollar state investments to build local advanced-manufacturing training facilities with cities, counties, community colleges and industry; no source reviewed connects Future48 to SmartStart.
Jeff Noel is publicly named in the SmartStart contributor roster and leads Kentucky's economic-development cabinet.

Kentucky records show Noel's cabinet operating through city, county, workforce, education, utility and regional-development partnerships on manufacturing projects; no source reviewed identifies those projects as SmartStart.

These three officials are stronger implementation bridges than general advisory participants because their institutions control funding, incentives, program administration or intergovernmental coordination.
data.framework: Authority mapping with a strict separation between contributor identity, institutional power, analogous programs and proven SmartStart transactions.
limitations: The LinkedIn roster does not provide affiliations or formal membership categories for each person.
No official WEF biography or initiative record independently confirms the three individual roster matches.
No reviewed local or state transaction document names SmartStart in connection with the highlighted implementation programs.
data.method: Resolve names from the public SmartStart contributor roster against official government leadership pages and official local-program records.
data.question: Which publicly named SmartStart contributors hold current authority over state and local workforce, school and manufacturing implementation channels?
data.scope: Michigan LEO, Arizona Commerce Authority and Kentucky Cabinet for Economic Development records reviewed through 2026-07-27.
unresolved: Whether any Skills in Sync awardee or Michigan school district is also a SmartStart pilot participant.
Whether ACA, Future48 or an Arizona community college exchanged curriculum, funding or implementation materials with SmartStart.
Whether Kentucky's cabinet, a local development council or a school/workforce partner entered a SmartStart-related agreement.
Whether the named officials personally participated in SmartStart workshops or delegated participation to their institutions.

summary: Three publicly named SmartStart contributors currently lead state institutions that fund or coordinate local workforce, school and manufacturing programs; no reviewed source proves those programs implement SmartStart.
title: SmartStart contributor overlap with state and local implementation authority
